ownership.contracts: signed wire shape, bounded roots, lifetime and path safety
ownership.control_plane: authenticated publication, signing, ETag, canary and rollback
ownership.daemon: signature verification, local root resolution, last-known-good cache and executable probes
ownership.desktop: bootstrap PATH and offline fallback only

http.failure: keep an unexpired last-known-good policy, otherwise use daemon-local fallback

cache.refresh: ETag conditional request with bounded backoff
cache.activation: verify signature, schema, time window and every rule before atomic replacement
cache.rollback: control-plane republishes a prior signed payload with a new monotonic revision

rollout: publish contracts package without runtime consumers
add control-plane endpoint disabled by default and verify 200/304/auth/signing
add daemon shadow fetch that validates and reports bounded result codes without changing discovery
canary policy activation for one profile with local fallback retained
expand activation after provider smoke and rollback drills
reduce Desktop hardcoded candidates to bootstrap-only in a later Desktop release

loop.observation: Provider search roots are compiled into Desktop and daemon, so vendor install-layout drift can require binary redistribution.
loop.hypothesis: A signed, bounded root-relative policy can move layout data to the control plane without allowing remote command or absolute-path injection.
loop.execute: Land the shared contract first, then add disabled publication, daemon shadow evaluation, canary activation and rollback as separate reviewed changes.
loop.evaluate: Contract tests reject unsafe paths and envelopes; integration tests prove 200/304, signature failure, expiry, cache fallback, canary and rollback behavior.
loop.retrospective: Only discovery data changes become server-managed; adapter protocol and parser changes still require daemon releases.
